column1: # fa.spoken.verbs.tsv -- the stems of the verbs the spoken pass (lib/spokenverb.py) can take apart.
# One row per verb.  Tab-separated, UTF-8, `#` starts a comment, the first row is the header.
#   past         the formal past stem (the infinitive without its nun)
#   spoken_present   the spoken present stems that differ from it, `|` between them (گ for گوی, ر for رو, ا and یا for آی)
#   spoken_past      the spoken past stems that differ (اومد for آمد, خوند for خواند)
#   formal       what the formal tables do their own way, `;` between: subj= the subjunctive's stem with its ب-, neg= the negative
#                present's, neg_past= the negative past's, imp= the imperative singular, negimp= the negative imperative singular
#   flags        bare (a present with no می-: داره), pre=<a preverb the stems stand behind: بر>, spoken_imp=<a spoken imperative
#                singular that is a word of its own: وایسا, for the formal بایست>, mi_stem=<a present stem with its می- written in: وایمیس>
#   src          note | hazm (iverbs.dat of Hazm, MIT: see fa.spoken.HAZM-LICENSE.txt) | note+hazm
# What is NOT here is made by rule from these (spokenverb.py): the spoken endings -e -in -an for -ad -id -and, the prefixes می- نمی- ب- ن-
# and the glide a prefix takes before a vowel, a bare imperative without ب, the ā → u of a stem that ends in -ān or -ānd (the causatives:
# رسون رسوند), and the loss of the t of -st before an ending (خواسم).  A form counts only if the formal form it makes is in the dictionary.
